== 9.4-A no ingestion
photos.sql:1: error: [9.4-A] photos is a file entity but lacks an ingestion-time field (when it arrived); a content hash or a dedup= declaration over the creation and ingestion times
    suggestion: Add captured_at timestamptz (from EXIF DateTimeOriginal with OffsetTimeOriginal, or document metadata) and ingested_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(). To deduplicate, add content_sha256 char(64) NOT NULL, or declare dedup=captured_at,ingested_at to compare by those times (§9.4).
1 error(s), 0 warning(s), 0 note(s) in 0 entities and 0 queries
== 9.4-B by name
photos.sql:1: error: [9.4-B] photos deduplicates files by name (the only uniqueness is on filename), so copies with different names duplicate and different files with the same name collide
    suggestion: Deduplicate by content, with UNIQUE (content_sha256) or UNIQUE (<scope>, content_sha256), or by creation and ingestion times with dedup=. Keep the object key unique as a storage address if needed, but never use the file name (§9.4).
1 error(s), 0 warning(s), 0 note(s) in 0 entities and 0 queries
== 9.4-B dedup name
photos.sql:1: error: [9.4-B] photos deduplicates files by name (dedup= names a file-name column), so copies with different names duplicate and different files with the same name collide
    suggestion: Deduplicate by content, with UNIQUE (content_sha256) or UNIQUE (<scope>, content_sha256), or by creation and ingestion times with dedup=. Keep the object key unique as a storage address if needed, but never use the file name (§9.4).
1 error(s), 0 warning(s), 0 note(s) in 0 entities and 0 queries
== 9.4-B no key
photos.sql:1: note: [9.4-B] photos enforces no uniqueness, so duplicates are caught only if ingestion code checks
    suggestion: Add UNIQUE (content_sha256), or UNIQUE (<scope>, content_sha256), so the database rejects duplicate files (§9.4).

== 9.8-A two ways
clicks.sql:2: warning: [9.8-A] clicks.clicked_at is timestamptz(0), which keeps 0 fractional digits, but the source provides 6
    suggestion: Use timestamptz with its default precision of 6, and truncate in queries instead (§9.8).
clicks.sql:3: warning: [9.8-A] clicks.shipped_at is named as an instant but is date, which keeps only the day
    suggestion: Store it as timestamptz (default precision 6), or rename it to a _date if only the day matters (§9.8).
